question: Explain the reverse charge mechanism under GST. When is the recipient liable to pay tax on reverse charge basis?
sources: CGST Act, 2017 - section 9(3) and 9(4) reverse charge
CGST Act, 2017 - section 2(98) reverse charge and section 2(82) output tax
CGST Act, 2017 - section 31(3) tax invoice by recipient

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Under reverse charge, the recipient of the supply, not the supplier, is liable to pay the tax.

points.label: Notified goods or services
points.description: The Government, on the GST Council's recommendation, notifies categories of goods or services on which the recipient pays tax, e.g. services of a goods transport agency or legal services by an advocate to a business entity.

points.label: Supplies from unregistered persons
points.description: The Government may notify a class of registered persons who must pay tax on reverse charge on specified goods or services received from unregistered suppliers.

points.label: Registration and invoice
points.description: A person liable to pay tax under reverse charge must register regardless of turnover, and a recipient buying from an unregistered supplier issues the invoice himself.

points.label: Payment and credit
points.description: Reverse charge tax must be paid in cash through the electronic cash ledger, not from input tax credit, because it is not 'output tax'; the recipient may then claim credit of that tax if otherwise eligible.
